data.narrative:
KoBold Metals is a Series C climate and energy technology company currently valued at $3.0B post-money, having raised over $1.0B to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of nine private frontier-tech peers in climate and energy, alongside one public comparable (LNZA).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchored to the $3.0B last post-money valuation, applies a typical 1.7x step-up multiplier for progression from Series C to the subsequent financing stage, yielding $5.0B. Peer-median valuation examined three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Redwood Materials ($6.0B, Series D), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C)—producing a median implied valuation of $1.0B across the sample, with a range of $700M to $6.0B.

The triangulated analysis across both methods supports a valuation range of $850M (low) to $5.8B (high), with a median estimate of $3.0B. The wide dispersion reflects uncertainty inherent in early-stage climate technology valuations, particularly the stage-progression method's sensitivity to assumed step-up multiples and the peer-median method's limited sample size and broad range of comparable stage and maturity. Key risks to valuation include execution on mineral exploration targets and commercialization timelines.
